source.title: EncQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Visual Encodings for Charts
source.authors: Kushin Mukherjee; Donghao Ren; Dominik Moritz; Yannick Assogba

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream chart-task accuracy across model sizes and reports that accuracy does not improve consistently with size, challenging downstream predictability by scale.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates chart-question accuracy, not held-out language-model cross-entropy, power-law fits, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Figure 8 reports the size comparisons; the paper's prose gives aggregate trends but does not enumerate the task-encoding pairs with each trend. Table 4 reports single-model accuracies and is not a size comparison.
record.test_reason: The study's own results compare chart-task accuracy across three InternVL2 sizes (2B, 8B, 26B). The authors argue explicitly that downstream accuracy often does not improve with size. This bears on V6 in a vision-language setting. No version about loss, fits or allocation is examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that chart-task error patterns cannot be explained by model size alone, since many task-encoding pairs do not improve or improve only sub-linearly with size. They add that advancing chart understanding needs targeted data or objectives rather than scaling alone. They also flag that the size analysis covers only one open and one closed model family.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures downstream visual chart-question accuracy across model sizes, rather than fitting pretraining-loss scaling laws or testing compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling pattern varies across chart task-encoding pairs; the authors say improvement is rarely present across all encoding channels.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
record.problems: The size analysis is limited to one open-source model family and one closed-source model family. Commercial-model parameter counts are unavailable, and the authors note limited generalizability. Figure 8 contains the detailed comparisons, while the prose only describes aggregate trends.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed task-encoding points in Figure 8 were not extracted because the plotted values are figure-only and the prose does not assign the aggregate trend to individual pairs. Table 4's individual model accuracies were left out because they do not themselves compare model sizes.

untested.parts: Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; any quantitative fit or prediction of downstream accuracy; controlled scale sweeps with fixed data and architecture; text-only language models.
All: no architecture-shape comparison at fixed size.
All: no power-law fits in any modality or regime.
All: no exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Table 3 lists reported ChartQA scores that rise with InternVL2 size (76.2, 83.3, 84.9). These are cited figures, not the study's own results, so they are not rows. Table 4 single-model accuracies are correctly left out. The study cites Kaplan et al. only as background. Its 'sub-linear' wording is qualitative, against a log-scale x-axis, with no fit.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of large-run loss from power laws fitted to small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures chart-task accuracy against model size, but does not test performance against pretraining loss or establish predictability for other downstream tasks.
Fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, fitting choices, and loss-curve bending.

rows.subject: InternVL2 family (InternVL2-2B, InternVL2-8B, InternVL2-26B)
rows.size_stated: 2B, 8B, and 26B; the two smaller models have 300M-parameter vision encoders and the largest has a 6B-parameter vision encoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared chart-task accuracy across three model sizes.

conditions.value: Multiple task-encoding pairs; the text does not identify each pair with its trend

rows.note: The authors state that many task-encoding pairs do not improve with increasing size or improve only sub-linearly, and that improvements are rarely seen across all encoding channels. This is an aggregate description; individual plotted values are not extracted.
rows.check: The state holds as an aggregate: the text says many task-encoding pairs show no or sub-linear gains, while some improve. Two caveats belong in the note. First, the sweep is not a controlled scaling series: the 26B model also scales its vision encoder from 300M to 6B parameters, and the backbones differ. Second, there are only three sizes, and no fit or loss is reported. Values are figure-only (Fig. 8 top).

rows.subject: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini
rows.size_stated: not stated; the paper says it does not have access to commercial-model parameter counts
rows.operation_detail: Compared chart-task accuracy for GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini.

conditions.value: Multiple task-encoding pairs; the text does not identify each pair with its trend

rows.note: Described as a coarser comparison; the authors' overall account says some task-encoding pairs improve with scale while many show no or sub-linear improvement.
rows.check: The parameter counts of GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini are unknown, and the authors call this comparison coarser. The text gives no specific trend for this pair beyond the shared Fig. 8 caption. The size gap cannot be placed on a scale axis, so it cannot show whether gains with scale are predictable.

relationships.condition: InternVL2 2B/8B/26B on EncQA chart task-encoding pairs
relationships.reason: Per the text and Fig. 8, many task-encoding pairs show no or only sub-linear accuracy gains with size, and gains rarely span all encodings; some pairs do improve (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Many task-encoding combinations showed absent or sublinear accuracy gains, and improvements rarely extended across every encoding.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
